answer: Cross-Epoch Divergence Scoring. Each identity's behaviour is fingerprinted per epoch across contextual features; a consistency score decays when consecutive epochs diverge beyond a calibrated bound. Divergence sends a ripple through the score, suppressing weight in later epochs. To fake persistence, a sybil must sustain a coherent behavioural fable across many epochs, not just one. Clones split across unrelated contexts are caught because their score growth never forms a stable vine of correlated epochs.
